data.name: Flank Steak Marinated
data.description: Marinated flank steak is a flavorful and tender grilled beef dish, enhanced with a zesty marinade of lime, soy, and herbs.
instructions: In a bowl, combine olive oil, soy sauce, lime juice, minced garlic, honey, ground black pepper, and chopped cilantro to create the marinade.
Place the flank steak in a resealable plastic bag or shallow dish and pour the marinade over the steak, ensuring it is well coated.
Seal the bag or cover the dish and refrigerate for at least 2 hours, preferably overnight, to allow the flavors to penetrate the meat.
Preheat the grill or grill pan to medium-high heat.
Remove the steak from the marinade, letting any excess drip off, and discard the remaining marinade.
Grill the flank steak for about 4-6 minutes per side for medium-rare, adjusting time based on thickness and desired doneness.
Once cooked, transfer the steak to a cutting board and let it rest for 5-10 minutes before slicing.
Slice the steak thinly against the grain to maximize tenderness and serve immediately.

data.name: London Broil
data.description: London Broil is a classic North American dish featuring marinated and grilled flank steak, known for its rich flavor and tender slices when properly prepared.
instructions: Marinate the beef flank steak with soy sauce, olive oil, Worcestershire sauce, minced garlic, lemon juice, brown sugar, black pepper, and dried oregano in a resealable bag or container for at least 4 hours or overnight in the refrigerator.
Preheat the grill or broiler to high heat.
Remove the steak from the marinade and pat it dry with paper towels.
Grill or broil the steak for about 4 to 6 minutes per side for medium-rare, depending on thickness.
Once cooked to desired doneness, remove the steak from heat and let it rest for 10 minutes.
Slice the steak thinly against the grain to ensure tenderness.
Serve slices with your preferred side dishes or garnish with fresh parsley if desired.

data.name: Pepper Steak (American)
data.description: Pepper steak is a classic American stir-fry dish featuring tender strips of flank steak cooked with colorful bell peppers and onions in a savory soy-based sauce. It's quick, delicious, and perfect served over rice.
instructions: Slice flank steak into thin strips against the grain.
In a bowl, combine soy sauce, oyster sauce, water, cornstarch, and sugar to make the sauce mixture.
Heat vegetable oil in a large skillet or wok over medium-high heat.
Add sliced steak to the skillet and stir-fry until browned and nearly cooked through, then remove from skillet and set aside.
In the same skillet, add a little more oil if needed, then stir-fry sliced green and red bell peppers and sliced onion until slightly tender but still crisp.
Add minced garlic and ginger, stir-fry for about 30 seconds until fragrant.
Return the steak to the skillet with the vegetables.
Pour the prepared sauce mixture into the skillet and stir well to combine all ingredients.
Cook and stir until the sauce thickens and coats the steak and vegetables evenly.
Adjust seasoning with salt and pepper as needed.
Serve hot, traditionally with steamed white rice.

data.name: Flank Steak with Shallots
data.description: A flavorful dish featuring grilled flank steak served with a rich shallot and red wine sauce, perfect for a satisfying main course.
instructions: Take the flank steak out of the refrigerator and let it rest at room temperature for about 20 minutes.
Preheat a large skillet or grill pan over medium-high heat.
Pat the flank steak dry with paper towels and season both sides generously with salt and pepper.
Add olive oil to the hot skillet, then place the flank steak in the pan.
Cook the steak for about 4-5 minutes on each side for medium-rare, or adjust the time to your preferred doneness.
Remove the steak from the skillet and set it aside to rest, loosely covered with foil.
In the same skillet, reduce the heat to medium and add butter.
Add the thinly sliced shallots and sauté until they are soft and caramelized, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic and cook for about 30 seconds until fragrant.
Pour in red wine and scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pan.
Let the sauce simmer and reduce by half, then stir in a bit of beef broth and continue to simmer until slightly thickened.
Return the steak to the skillet to warm for a minute, spooning some shallot sauce over it.
Slice the flank steak thinly against the grain, arrange on a serving platter, and spoon the shallot sauce with shallots on top.
Garnish with fresh parsley and serve immediately.

data.name: Carne Asada Burrito
data.description: Carne Asada Burrito is a flavorful Mexican dish featuring marinated grilled steak wrapped in a flour tortilla with rice, beans, and fresh toppings.
instructions: Marinate the steak by combining lime juice, olive oil, garlic, cumin, chili powder, salt, and pepper in a bowl, then coat the steak and let it marinate for at least 30 minutes.
Preheat a grill or grill pan over high heat and cook the steak for 4-5 minutes per side until desired doneness is reached.
Remove the steak from the grill and let it rest for 5 minutes before slicing thinly against the grain.
Warm the flour tortilla on the grill or in a skillet until pliable.
Place the sliced carne asada in the center of the tortilla.
Add toppings such as cooked rice, black beans, chopped cilantro, diced onion, sliced avocado, and sour cream if desired.
Fold the sides of the tortilla and roll it up tightly to form a burrito.
Serve the burrito with salsa or hot sauce on the side.

data.name: Carne Asada (Grilled Beef)
data.description: Carne Asada is a traditional Mexican dish featuring marinated and grilled flank steak, known for its smoky, citrusy, and spiced flavor profile, perfect for tacos or as a main entree.
instructions: Combine lime juice, olive oil, garlic, cilantro, cumin, oregano, salt, black pepper, and chili powder in a bowl to prepare the marinade.
Place flank steak in a shallow dish or resealable plastic bag and pour the marinade over the meat, making sure it is well coated.
Cover the dish or seal the bag and refrigerate for at least 1 hour, preferably 4 hours or overnight, for the flavors to infuse.
Preheat the grill to high heat and oil the grates to prevent sticking.
Remove the steak from the marinade and shake off excess liquid.
Grill the steak for about 4 to 6 minutes per side for medium-rare, or cook longer to desired doneness.
Transfer the steak to a cutting board and let it rest for 5 minutes before slicing.
Slice the steak thinly against the grain and serve with warm tortillas, salsa, and optional toppings.

data.name: Sonora Carne Asada (Sonoran Grilled Steak)
data.description: Sonora Carne Asada is a traditional Mexican grilled flank steak marinated with citrus juices and spices, known for its vibrant flavors and tender texture typical of the Sonora region.
instructions: Place the flank steak in a large shallow dish or resealable plastic bag.
In a bowl, combine lime juice, orange juice, olive oil, garlic, cumin, salt, black pepper, chili powder, and chopped cilantro to make the marinade.
Pour the marinade over the steak, ensuring it is well coated. Cover and refrigerate for at least 2 hours or overnight for best flavor.
Preheat a grill or grill pan over high heat.
Remove the steak from the marinade and discard the marinade.
Grill the steak for about 4-6 minutes per side for medium-rare, or until desired doneness is reached.
Remove the steak from the grill and let it rest for 5-10 minutes before slicing.
Slice the steak thinly against the grain and serve.
Optionally, serve with warm tortillas, grilled onions, fresh salsa, and lime wedges.

data.name: Northern Mexico Carne Asada Party
data.description: This Northern Mexico Carne Asada Party recipe features marinated grilled flank steak served in warm corn tortillas with fresh toppings, capturing the traditional flavors of Northern Mexican celebrations.
instructions: In a large bowl, combine lime juice, orange juice, olive oil, minced garlic, chopped jalapeno, chopped cilantro, ground cumin, chili powder, smoked paprika, salt, and black pepper to make the marinade.
Add flank steak to the marinade and coat evenly. Cover and refrigerate for at least 2 hours, preferably overnight, to allow flavors to develop.
Preheat grill to high heat. Remove steak from marinade and pat dry with paper towels.
Grill steak for 4-6 minutes per side or until desired doneness is reached.
Remove steak from grill and let it rest for 5 minutes before slicing thinly against the grain.
Warm corn tortillas on the grill or skillet until pliable.
Serve the sliced carne asada on warm tortillas with diced onion, chopped cilantro, fresh lime wedges, and optional toppings like guacamole, salsa, and radish slices for a festive party.
Accompany with side dishes such as grilled peppers and onions, Mexican rice, and refried beans to complete the Northern Mexico carne asada party experience.

data.name: Asador (Grill Restaurant Feast)
data.description: Asador is a traditional grill feast typically served at Argentinian or Uruguayan restaurants featuring various grilled meats and vegetables served with chimichurri sauce and fresh bread.
instructions: Preheat the grill to medium-high heat to ensure it is hot and ready for cooking.
Season the meat cuts (such as short ribs, flank steak, and chorizo) generously with salt and pepper on both sides.
Place the meat pieces on the grill and cook, turning occasionally, until they reach the desired doneness, typically 4-6 minutes per side for medium rare beef.
Grill the vegetables (such as bell pepper, onion, and tomato) alongside the meat, brushing them lightly with olive oil to prevent sticking and enhance flavor.
Remove the meat and vegetables from the grill and let the meat rest for a few minutes to retain juices.
Slice the grilled meat against the grain into thin strips for tender bites.
Arrange the grilled meat and vegetables on a large serving platter, offering chimichurri sauce on the side for dipping.
Serve the feast with crusty bread and a simple salad to complement the rich flavors of the grilled items.

data.name: Mongolian Beef
data.description: Mongolian Beef is a popular Chinese-American dish featuring tender strips of beef stir-fried with a savory and sweet soy-based sauce and green onions. It's known for its rich flavor and quick cooking time.
instructions: Slice the beef thinly against the grain and set aside.
In a bowl, mix soy sauce, brown sugar, and water until the sugar dissolves to create the sauce.
Heat vegetable oil in a wok or large skillet over high heat.
Add the sliced beef and stir-fry until browned and cooked through, then remove from the pan and set aside.
In the same pan, add additional oil if needed and sauté minced garlic and grated ginger until fragrant.
Pour in the prepared sauce and bring it to a simmer until it thickens slightly.
Return the cooked beef to the pan and toss to coat evenly with the sauce.
Add sliced green onions and cook for another minute to combine flavors.
Serve hot over steamed rice.
